title: DAS-ILU: A Distributed Asynchronous Parallel ILU Factorization Based on Domain Decomposition
problem: Incomplete LU (ILU) factorization as a preconditioner is computationally expensive and poorly parallelizable due to data dependencies. Existing parallel ILU methods have high cross-processor communication overhead.
motivation: ILU preconditioning is widely used in iterative solvers for structural mechanics, CFD, and reservoir simulation, but current parallel implementations suffer from synchronization bottlenecks and communication overhead.
method: DAS-ILU partitions computational domain into independently processed interior nodes and asynchronously updated separator nodes. Reduces cross-processor dependencies and separator size by half. Uses optimized data exchange patterns and extends to block-structured matrices.
key_novelty: Asynchronous domain decomposition approach for ILU that decouples interior computation from separator updates, halving separator size and reducing communication.
contributions: 2.07x speedup over Chow-Patel fine-grained parallel ILU
Evaluation on structural mechanics, CFD, and reservoir simulation
Support for block-structured sparse matrices via exact block inversions
Robustness on challenging nonsymmetric and indefinite systems
limitations: Full-text not available; analysis based on abstract. Scalability characteristics not detailed. GPU acceleration not discussed.
primary_theme: Scalable parallel preconditioning for distributed sparse linear systems
